validated_results.title: Decreased incidence of prostate cancer with selenium supplementation: results of a double-blind cancer prevention trial.
validated_results.reason: Double-blind randomized trial of 200 microg/day selenium supplementation reporting prostate cancer incidence as a secondary endpoint with a relative risk and case counts.

extraction.population: Men with a history of either a basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 974 men with a history of either a basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma were randomized to either a daily supplement of 200 microg of selenium or a placebo. Patients were treated for a mean of 4.5 years and followed for a mean of 6.5 years.

cases.excerpt: There were 13 prostate cancer cases in the selenium-treated group and 35 cases in the placebo group (relative risk, RR=0.37, P=0.002). Restricting the analysis to the 843 patients with initially normal levels of prostate-specific antigen (< or = 4 ng/mL), only four cases were diagnosed in the selenium-treated group and 16 cases were diagnosed in the placebo group after a 2 year treatment lag, (RR=0.26 P=0.009).
